dossier.public_summary: The dip changes from practically nothing to ~3000 ppm from sector to sector and from transit to transit in the same data, opposite to a planet which should have a steady depth. It is carried by just a few outlier transits and shows no stable on-target signature. This is best explained by non-repeating, variable blending or noise, not a planet on the target star.

reasons.why: Depth is not constant between sectors; true variation confirmed by sector_depths_by_source changes_within_a_source, ruling out a stable on-target planet and pointing to a blend or noise.
Variation persists even within a single light-curve product (SPOC 2-min), so it is not a pipeline calibration difference; the dip depth genuinely changes with aperture/epoch.
reasons.value: verdict changes_within_a_source, SPOC 2-min p_constant 1.4051779495738654e-25, SPOC 2-min depth 659+/-51 ppm vs TESS-SPOC depth 101+/-45 ppm with 5 vs 3 sectors

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent and dominated by a few very deep outliers in sectors 51 and 26; the signal does not repeat at a consistent depth as a planet on the target should.

reasons.why: Centroid difference imaging failed, so on-target location cannot confirm a planet; combined with depth instability and non-repeating transits there is no positive planet evidence.
